newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Anaconda, Central Bore settle dispute.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Anaconda, Central Bore settle dispute.

text.p: Nickel explorers Central Bore Nickel NL and Anaconda Nickel NL said late on Wednesday they had settled their legal actions relating to the Murrin Murrin tenements in Western Australia.

The dispute relats to the acquisition of mining leases M39/315, M39/316, M39/317 and prospecting licences 39/2973 and 39/3295, known as the Murrin Murrin tenements, by Anaconda from Central Bore in September 1995.
-- Central Bore to discontinue Supreme Court proceedings against Anaconda.

-- Anaconda to immediately exercise its option under the original sale agreement with the payment of A$8 million consideration in two parts - A$4.5 million of which A$2 million can be satisfied by issue of Anaconda shares with payment to be made by February 1, 1997, and A$3.5 million by February 1, 1998.

-- Anaconda to pay an additional A$16.25 million to Central Bore once the Murrin Murrin project has completed a normal banker's acceptance test and after the first 12 months operational period during which the the real average nickel price as quoted by the London Metal Exchange exceeds US$3.50 per pound. Both these paymenst are subject to inflation adjustment
based on the U.S. consumer price index.
The companies said court proceedings were originally instituted as a derivative action by Central Bore shareholder Peter Salter and subsequently adopted by Central Bore itself.
In the proceedings, Central Bore alleged Anaconda acted improperly at the time it acquired the Murrin Murrin Tenements from Central Bore.

Anaconda said that while it denied all allegations and was confident that its actions would be vindicated by the court, the companies had agreed to settle the dispute so as to avoid unnecessary costly litigation and to facilitate early
The Murrin Murrin project is forecast to produce 100 million pounds of nickel per year once fully operational in mid-1998.
